annotations.text:
Four layouts of one model.
They differ on what you see at once: A shows the whole week for every metric, B shows one metric properly, C shows one metric at a time without hiding the rest, D shows one day at a time.

Shared pieces.
Both of these work with whichever option you pick — the calculation panel behind a metric, and the rule that a position inherits the squad number until you type over it.

Three ways to fit the calculation into the matrix.
Everything else on these three is identical to Option A — only the metric column changes. A1 shows every setting, A2 opens the row in place, A3 states the window once for the squad and flags the exceptions.

A2 and A3 combine: squad default in the scope bar, expanding row for the metric that needs its own.

CSV as a second way in, not a replacement.
The sheet is the same grid as Option A: one row per squad, position and metric, one column per gameday. The preview screens follow the existing three-step import flow in the Sessions file.

The move that makes this worth building is the round trip — export what is on screen, edit in Excel, import it back. Setting up eight squads is a copy-paste in a spreadsheet instead of eight passes through the UI.
